idiom_name: module-level Hash with register/lookup module methods
implementation_notes: A module constant Hash with register/lookup module methods is the registry, and the Hash is the store; Rails ships the same shape as ActiveModel::Type::Registry (an @registrations hash with register and lookup). What replaces the classic Registry class is a module plus two methods - instance management is left to the module's own constant (or a class-level @registry instance variable). A class is justified when several registries must coexist: ActiveModel implements initialize_copy so dup gives an independent copy, which is exactly the case a bare module cannot express.
pitfalls: Require/load order decides what is registered: a file that is never required registers nothing, so discovery must be explicit (or driven by Zeitwerk autoloading).
Under Rails development reloading, holding class objects pins the old constants after a reload; store names and resolve lazily via constantize/const_get (Rails' own registries do exactly this).
Hash mutation is not thread-safe: MRI's GVL usually hides it, but JRuby and TruffleRuby will race, so freeze after boot or synchronize registration.

dup on a registry object shallow-copies only the instance variables - the registrations hash is still shared unless initialize_copy deep-copies it (ActiveModel::Type::Registry implements initialize_copy for this).
